pattern_name: Modals of past deduction (must/might/can't have + participle)
pattern_name_ar: أفعال الاستنتاج في الماضي (must/might/can't have + التصريف الثالث)
formula: must have + participle (sure it happened) · might/may/could have + participle (possible) · can't/couldn't have + participle (impossible)
formula_visual: [He must have forgotten] // [She might have missed it] // [It can't have been him]
when_to_use: To make deductions about the PAST based on present evidence. must have = I'm sure it happened. might/may/could have = it possibly happened. can't/couldn't have = it's impossible. All take 'have + past participle'.
when_to_use_ar: للاستنتاج عن الماضي بناءً على دليل حاضر. must have متأكد، might/may/could have ممكن، can't/couldn't have مستحيل. كلها + have + التصريف الثالث.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Learners confuse 'mustn't have' with "can't have" — in English 'mustn't' means prohibition, never impossibility. They also write 'must of' because that is exactly how /mʌstəv/ sounds, and they mix this up with the regret meaning of 'should have'.

examples.en: He must have forgotten the meeting.
She might have missed the train.
It can't have been him; he was abroad.
examples.ar: مستحيل أن يكون هو؛ كان بالخارج

examples.en: The lights are off, so they must have gone out.
examples.ar: الأنوار مطفأة، فلا بد أنهم خرجوا

common_errors.explanation: For impossibility use "can't have"; 'mustn't' means prohibition.

common_errors.correct: He must have forgotten. / He must've forgotten.
common_errors.explanation: 'must've' is 'must have'; 'must of' is never correct in writing.

common_errors.correct: He must have forgotten the meeting.
common_errors.explanation: Past deduction needs 'have + past participle' after the modal.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: It ___ (can't / be) him; he was abroad.
The lights are off, so they ___ (must / go) out.

quick_rule: must have (sure) · might/may/could have (maybe) · can't/couldn't have (impossible). Always + past participle. Never 'mustn't have' for impossibility.
quick_rule_ar: must have (متأكد) · might/could have (ربما) · can't have (مستحيل). دائمًا + التصريف الثالث. ولا تستخدم mustn't have للاستحالة.
mnemonic: Sure → must've · Maybe → might've · Impossible → can't have (NOT mustn't have).
connect_to_speaking: In accent week 10 you drilled /mʌstəv/, /maɪtəv/ and /kɑːntəv/ with three different confidence tones. Your certainty must be audible — the same words said flat lose the meaning.
